sections.h2: What does a fast sale look like in Bonita Springs?
sections.html:
A quick Bonita Springs sale usually means a cash buyer who purchases as-is, while a listing leans on showings, inspections and buyer financing. Many owners here are dealing with storm repairs, a seasonal second home or an estate, and each of those affects the route you pick.

  • Cash buyer: takes the house as it stands, and you pick the closing day together.
  • Agent listing: more exposure, with repairs and lender dates in the schedule.
  • Owner sale: you run the contract and the recording.

Whichever route you choose, Lee County's property appraiser, tax collector and clerk all play a part, so start with the property record for your address.

sections.h2: What is the history behind Bonita Springs homes?
sections.html:
Bonita Springs began as a settlement called Survey, named after Army Corps of Engineers surveyors who camped on the upper Imperial River in the 1870s. A post office opened in 1901, the Eagle Hotel was serving hunting and fishing visitors by 1910, and developers later renamed the town to sell it better.

Barron Collier extended his rail line south in the early 1920s, and the Tamiami Trail opened in 1928, bringing a land boom and a brief first incorporation. Roadside attractions followed, with the Everglades Reptile Gardens opening in 1936 and a greyhound track in December 1957. The city says air conditioning, Interstate 75, a nearby major airport and the US 41 bypass drove growth in the 1980s and 1990s, bringing malls, offices and golf courses. Residents voted to incorporate again in 1999.

That layered growth explains why a Bonita Springs street can mix older homes with golf course communities, so the age of your house shapes what a buyer will inspect.

sections.h2: What does Hurricane Ian mean for selling a Bonita Springs house?
sections.html:
If your house was damaged, report it to the Lee County Property Appraiser, because the new value is set as of January 1 following the event and the damage is factored into it. The appraiser's hurricane page asks owners to email hurricaneupdate@leepa.org or use its reporting link.

The page explains that residential owners can apply for a partial tax refund depending on the extent of damage and whether they could use the property, with details in section 197.319 of the Florida Statutes. It adds that a rebuild that changes the property significantly will likely raise its value, while a rebuild similar to the old one should have a minimal effect. Permits are still required under each jurisdiction's process, and the FEMA 50 percent rule applies to substantial repairs, so ask the city's building staff what applies before you spend money on a house you plan to sell.

  • Condominiums do not get a tax roll value letter, because the appraiser does not split land and building value for a whole complex.
  • A private appraisal of the entire complex is the route the appraiser suggests for condo owners working with their association.
  • Do not register to vote or get a driver license elsewhere while repairing, or the homestead exemption could be jeopardized; changing your mailing address is fine.

sections.h2: How do Lee County property taxes work when I sell?
sections.html:
The appraiser values property each January 1, the tax collector bills in November, and a sale resets the next owner's assessed value to market on the following January 1. The homestead exemption is up to $50,000 and needs a filing by March 1, and Save Our Homes caps yearly increases at the lower of 3 percent or the CPI change, which the state shows as 2.7 percent for 2026.

Lee County tax steps that touch a Bonita Springs sale, with state deadlines
StepRule
Value dateJanuary 1 each year
Exemption filingMarch 1 with the property appraiser
Notice of proposed taxesMailed in August
BillsSent in November
DelinquentApril 1

Seasonal owners should note that homestead is lost if the home is rented or stops being the permanent residence. A value challenge goes to the clerk within 25 days of the August notice.

sections.h2: What taxes apply to a Bonita Springs deed?
sections.html:
Florida charges documentary stamp tax of 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed in Lee County, and every party to the deed is liable to the state. The clerk collects it at recording.

The clerk's recording charges are set by statute and are per page, and the deed needs two subscribing witnesses. A personal representative's deed under a probated will is listed by the state as not taxable, and a deed that only discharges a mortgage between spouses on homestead can be exempt.

sections.h2: What if the house is inherited, rented or facing foreclosure?
sections.html:
Each situation has a state clock. An estate of $150,000 or less, or one where the owner died over two years ago, can use summary administration.

For a tenant behind on rent, Florida allows a written three day notice that skips weekends and court holidays. A foreclosure sale follows judgment by 20 to 35 days.

If taxes are delinquent, Florida sells tax certificates by June 1, and a holder may apply for a tax deed after two years. Ask the Lee County Tax Collector for a payoff before you pick a closing day.

sections.h2: What are the steps to close a Bonita Springs sale?
sections.html:
1. Look up the parcel on the Lee County Property Appraiser site and note exemptions and any damage report.
  2. Request a lender payoff and a tax balance from the tax collector.
  3. Check city permit records for open or unpermitted work.
  4. Compare a listing, a private sale and a cash offer after taxes and recording charges.
  5. Sign the deed before two witnesses and record it with the Lee County clerk.

faqs.q: Is Bonita Springs in Lee County?
faqs.a: Yes. The city's property is assessed by the Lee County Property Appraiser. The city incorporated in 1999 after an earlier brief incorporation in the 1920s.

faqs.q: Do I need to tell the appraiser about hurricane damage?
faqs.a: Yes. The appraiser asks owners to report damage because the new value is set as of the January 1 after the event. Residential owners may also apply for a partial refund under section 197.319.

faqs.q: Can I keep my homestead while repairing a storm-damaged house?
faqs.a: Yes, if you tell the appraiser you intend to repair or rebuild and make it your permanent residence. Avoid actions like registering to vote or getting a license in another county or state.

faqs.q: What is the doc stamp rate in Lee County?
faqs.a: 70 cents per $100 of consideration on a deed. All parties to the deed are liable to the state regardless of who agrees to pay.

faqs.q: What happens to my homestead exemption after I sell?
faqs.a: It goes with you and does not stay on the house. The next owner files for their own by March 1, and the property is reassessed at market value the following January 1.
